assumptions: kappa>=1; actual twice continuous Frechet differentiability of V; simultaneous Hessian lower and upper quadratic bounds at every x,v; genuine measurability of eta and y; pointwise strict positivity of eta. No p, G, K or integrability certificate is supplied as a hypothesis. No topology on S, boundedness of eta/y, lower dimensional cutoff, or positivity of the final signed scalar is imposed.
conclusion: Existence of one measurable p solving the implicit gradient equation; quadratic lower growth of literal F at p and exact iff characterization of the only point with value at most F(p); same-eta nonexpansive dependence of p on y; measurability and same-eta pair estimate for literal G; existence of one Markov kernel equal at every s to the Gaussian pushforward under G(s, .); actual vector first-moment integrability; for every a and signed scalar r, actual centered exponential integrability and upper bound exp(eta(s)*r^2*||a||^2/2).
constant_dependencies: F uses eta(s)^(-1)/2. Growth coefficient is (kappa^(-1)+eta(s)^(-1))/2. The p Lipschitz coefficient is exactly 1. The G bound has coefficients 1 on ||y(s)-y(t)|| and sqrt(eta(s)) on ||z-w||, under same-eta equality. The exponential coefficient is eta(s)*||a||^2/2 times r^2, with no kappa or dimension factor. kappa>=1 and eta>0 exclude inverse singularities in their appearances; zero vectors, zero signed scalar and zero dimension remain included.
domains: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product normed additive commutative space with Borel measurable structure and may have dimension zero. S has only a measurable-space structure. V:E->R; kappa in R with kappa>=1; eta:S->R with eta(s)>0; y,p:S->E; F:S->E->R; G:S x E->E; K is a measurable kernel S->measures on E. All Hessian points/directions, optimization points, output points and noise variables range over the full E.
objects: E and its canonical Gaussian gamma; arbitrary measurable space S; potential V; real kappa; measurable parameter eta; measurable center y; literal let-bound F; existential measurable optimizer p; literal let-bound G using this p; existential Markov kernel K; its vector mean m_s; testing vector a and signed scalar r.
quantifiers: Universal E,S and structures, V,kappa, stated hypotheses, eta,y and their hypotheses; then define F; then exists one function p satisfying all its conjuncts; then define G from that same p; then exists one kernel K satisfying all kernel and integral conjuncts. Hessian bounds: forall x,v. Stationarity: forall s. Growth and unique minimizer equivalence: forall s,z. p estimate: forall s,t, eta(s)=eta(t) implies bound. G estimate: forall s,t,z,w, eta(s)=eta(t) implies bound. Law identity: forall s. Identity integrability: forall s. Centered exponential integrability and bound: forall s, forall a in E, forall r in R.
reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product normed additive commutative space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure (dimension zero permitted), every measurable space S, every twice continuously Frechet differentiable function V:E->R, and every real kappa with 1<=kappa, suppose that for all x,v in E the actual Hessian satisfies
kappa^(-1)*||v||^2 <= D^2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
For every measurable eta:S->R and measurable y:S->E such that eta(s)>0 for every s, define the actual function F(s,x)=V(x)+(eta(s)^(-1)/2)*||x-y(s)||^2.
There exists a single measurable function p:S->E such that all the following hold simultaneously:
(1) For every s, p(s)+eta(s)*gradient V(p(s))=y(s), where the gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual Frechet derivative for the given real inner product.
(2) For every s in S and z in E,
F(s,p(s))+((kappa^(-1)+eta(s)^(-1))/2)*||z-p(s)||^2 <= F(s,z),
and F(s,z)<=F(s,p(s)) if and only if z=p(s).
(3) For every s,t in S with eta(s)=eta(t), ||p(s)-p(t)||<=||y(s)-y(t)||.
With this same p, define the actual function G:S x E->E by G(s,z)=gradient V(p(s)+sqrt(eta(s))*z). G is measurable for the product measurable structure, and for every s,t in S and z,w in E with eta(s)=eta(t),
||G(s,z)-G(t,w)||<=||y(s)-y(t)||+sqrt(eta(s))*||z-w||.
There exists a single measurable probability kernel K from S to E such that for every s, K(s) is exactly the pushforward of the canonical centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure gamma on E under z->G(s,z). For every s, the identity function w->w is Bochner integrable under K(s). Writing m_s=Integral_E v dK(s)(v), for every vector a in E and every real scalar r, the function w->exp(r*<a,w-m_s>) is Bochner integrable under K(s), and
Integral_E exp(r*<a,w-m_s>) dK(s)(w) <= exp(eta(s)*r^2*||a||^2/2).
The exponential center m_s is the own vector mean under that same output law K(s). All vectors and noise variables range over the full E; r has either sign and may be zero, and a may be zero. Equal eta is required in both pairwise estimates, but is not a restriction on the pointwise kernel or exponential conclusions. K is the law of the Gaussian-input gradient output G, without any additional transition-law identification.
scopes: F is fixed before p is chosen and is not an existential energy witness. All p conditions share the same function p. G is fixed after p is chosen and is not an existential output witness. K is chosen after p and G, and all output-law and integrability assertions share this K. The equality eta(s)=eta(t) is required separately in both pair estimates; neither estimate covers arbitrary unequal eta. The final scalar variable named t in Lean is locally rebound within forall (a:E) (t:R) and is independent of the earlier pairwise point t in S; it is rendered r here to disambiguate. The vector mean is the integral of v under K(s), shared as the center in the exponential integrability and bound. The Hessian two inequalities are conjunctive for each identical x,v.
